learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
The student will handle all transmission elements of a machine, and will be able to analyze their kinematic and dynamic behavior, considering each of their elements as rigid bodies.

syllabus_topics: Kinematic Analysis of Mechanisms. Analytical and Graphical Methods.
Basic Concepts of Work and Energy Applied to Mechanisms.
teaching_methods: Theoretical-practical content sessions in teaching and work groups (60 hours)
Workgroup sessions in computer labs for manual problem solving and computer implementation for advanced analysis and simulations
Monitoring of autonomous student work with virtual classroom tools
Use of interactive material from the Mechanical Engineering Area server

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (or practical exam in extraordinary call)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.8 * final exam grade + 0.2 * (practical work grade or practical exam grade). It is a necessary but not sufficient requirement to pass the subject to obtain a grade of 4 or higher out of 10 in the final exam. For basic competencies (CB1, CB2), a grade of at least 5 out of 10 is required in the practical work or the practical exam. In the extraordinary call, students who passed a part (final exam or practical work) in the ordinary call will keep that grade and only need to retake the failed part. If the practical work is not submitted/presented or fails in the ordinary call, specific questions about it will be included in the extraordinary exam.
